message: nat_console::config::get_config_info is named like an accessor but its callee graph has effects: reads-world
why: get_config_info reads /lib/systemd/system/nat.service off disk and clap-parses its ExecStart line on the fall-through path (config.rs:37 -> 44-89); the effect is buried one call deep behind a getter name, which is the lie #6 is about.

message: nat_console::config::get_nftables_rules is named like an accessor but its callee graph has effects: spawns, writes-process
why: get_nftables_rules forks four /usr/sbin/nft subprocesses (174, 184, 197, 210); a get_-named free function that spawns four processes per call misstates its cost to every caller, and both handlers call it once per request with no cache.

message: nat_console::handlers::get_config is named like an accessor but its callee graph has effects: reads-world
why: axum route handler, registered at server.rs:55 as `get(get_config).post(save_config)`: the name mirrors the HTTP method, not an accessor contract, and reading the config it serves is the route's whole purpose. Renaming it would desync the route table.

message: nat_console::handlers::get_rules is named like an accessor but its callee graph has effects: spawns, writes-process
why: axum route handler for `GET /rules` (server.rs:57); the spawn effect is inherited wholly from get_nftables_rules, already flagged at config.rs:170, so the honest-name fix belongs at the callee. Same HTTP-verb naming as the get_config row.

message: nat_console::handlers::get_rules_json is named like an accessor but its callee graph has effects: spawns, writes-process
why: axum route handler for `GET /api/rules` (server.rs:56); same inherited spawn as the get_rules row, third report of the one defect at config.rs:170. Handler names are fixed by the route they serve.
